markdown_report:
**Proposal: coverage-first, budget-matched diagnostic guidance.** At 10% research progress, establish whether a frozen diagnostic policy improves search before expanding perturbations. Treat its action mappings as hypotheses, not calibrated predictors of improvement.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) All four earlier panels were missing. Empty perturbation records establish missing execution, not insensitivity. (2) Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl show higher training-pair ordering errors. This motivates competitor analysis without establishing validation weakness. (3) Effective-rank fractions near 0.99 provide no obvious evidence of broad collapse. Ranking and history-use interventions therefore deserve testing before collapse remedies.

**Insights from related work.** (1) DeepMutation supports verified faults and intact controls [1]. Fault detection does not validate intervention selection. (2) Sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog comparisons [2]. Keep diagnostic ranks separate from pinned HR@10. (3) SASRec ablations are dataset-dependent [3]; HGN and SLi-Rec support gated interest modeling, without establishing this residual [7–8]. (4) HPO methodology supports random-search comparators, complete cost traces, and selection-bias warnings [4–6]. Search repetitions measure search randomness, not training robustness.

**Framework and directions.** Organize execution, measurement, action specification, and prospective selection:

| Layer | Evidence | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Coverage | Routes, histories, twenty recommendations | Did diagnosis execute? |
| Calibration | Identity, permutation, verified mutations | Are intended faults detected? |
| Ranking | Uniform versus hard-pool ordering | Which competitors remain unresolved? |
| Action mapping | Frozen rules and subsequent gains | Does evidence predict useful interventions? |
| Selection | Budget-matched incumbent curves | Does guidance improve search? |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coverage and mutation calibration [1] | 4/7/4 | Auditable integration; reusable; bounded | Established principles; indirect gains; model hooks |
| Hard-pool rank audit [2] | 4/7/4 | Focused; actionable; existing scoring | Familiar; uncertain transfer; sparse transitions |
| Budget-matched guidance experiment [3–6] | 4/7/7 | Direct policy test; reusable; finite menu | Limited novelty; noisy outcomes; complex accounting |
| More negatives with gBCE [9] | 2/7/4 | Strong loss comparator; promising; localized | Established; gains uncertain; extra scoring |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the guidance experiment, with an independently fixed strong SASRec incumbent. Compare diagnostic guidance, random search, and a prospectively randomized guidance placebo over identical configurations: unchanged SASRec, gated recent-history residual, and uniform/transition-negative mixture. Specify gate initialization, normalization, sampling, thresholds, and action mappings before outcomes. Fault calibration checks instrumentation only.

Repair routing first; use supplied users or deterministically select five real training users/category. Generate unseen full-catalog recommendations for all twenty. Give arms equal total GPU budgets, including diagnostics, validation, failures, and unfinished trials. Random search uses the same configuration distribution. Shuffle complete guidance blocks while preserving action frequencies; four routes allow at most 24 permutations. Report ineffective shuffles; route exchangeability is unestablished.

Publish incumbent macro validation HR@10 versus cumulative GPU-seconds, category outcomes, endpoint scores, and separate wall/CPU/LLM costs. Never backfill late results. Repeat whole searches only within the shared budget, pairing search seeds across arms. Freeze final selection before host-held-out evaluation; repeated validation creates optimism. No improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Prospectively test whether coverage-verified, frozen diagnostic guidance improves anytime and endpoint validation-selected SASRec performance relative to random search and a block-randomized guidance placebo under equal total GPU budgets.
idea.motivation: Earlier runs omitted the required user panels, while training-only ranking errors varied without obvious broad embedding collapse. The immediate gap is evidence that diagnostics help choose useful interventions. Mutation detection establishes instrumentation sensitivity, whereas action-selection usefulness requires observing subsequent intervention gains. At 10% progress, a small predefined experiment is preferable to learning a policy from four routes or expanding an unvalidated diagnostic suite.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the metrics/metric_definitions return structure. Keep view.model as the actual trained module and adapt item_emb, log2feats and predict_score consistently. Retain user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility hooks without accessing unavailable fields. Resolve all four routes explicitly. Use supplied panel IDs when available; otherwise deterministically select five eligible real training users/category using a local seed-42 generator over sorted IDs. Freeze and record IDs, eligibility, history hashes, mapping/checkpoint hashes and settings across arms. Selection fallback is an implementation choice, not evidence of representativeness. Missing coverage is a failure, never zero sensitivity. Produce full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for all twenty users, excluding each user's complete original training history. Chunk scoring, break diagnostic ties by item ID, and read right-aligned sequence features at the final slot. Preserve individual module flags and Python/NumPy/torch RNG states; do not consume the live training iterator. If separate margin batches are needed, retain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors and an independent generator.

Use only training histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions. Ownership, compatibility, current utility, review attributes and simulator traits remain unobserved unless explicitly established by permitted evidence. Preserve matched perturbation support checks, fixed candidate pools and explicit missingness; do not interpret stability as accuracy. Identity, candidate-permutation and bounded verified mutation checks assess instrumentation. Positional removal need not harm performance, and causal leakage checks must examine earlier representations under suffix edits. Tied item embeddings complicate mutation attribution. Mutation results must not be presented as evidence that a recency or sampling intervention will help.

Before new outcomes, publish a versioned configuration manifest defining all baseline hyperparameters, action configurations, diagnostic cutoffs, missing-data behavior, action-priority mappings, tie rules and stopping conditions. A concrete minimal residual configuration is k=5 causal nonpadding items ending at position t, including its current input item, with no future positions; r_t is their masked mean item embedding. Define h'_t = h_t + sigmoid(b) * LayerNorm(r_t), with an independent learned scalar b initialized to -4, LayerNorm scale 1 and bias 0. Use h'_t consistently for training and inference, with padding masked. This is a proposed implementation choice, not a published HGN or SLi-Rec architecture. If expanded, preregister last-item-only, masked recent mean, fixed residual and learned-gate ablations rather than adding them after outcomes.

For the sampling action, fix rho=0.25 and preserve the baseline's negative count. Build directed adjacent-transition counts from training interactions only. At a training position ending with item i, the hard pool contains observed successors of i excluding padding, the positive target and all items in that user's complete training history. Draw uniformly from the hard pool with probability rho and otherwise uniformly from the eligible catalog; fall back to uniform when the hard pool is empty. Skip and count positions with no eligible negatives. This mixture is an implementation choice, not GNNO. Transition candidates can be false negatives, so report pool coverage and target-popularity distributions and avoid assuming harder sampling improves HR@10. Keep gSASRec/gBCE as a separately declared alternative rather than silently changing negative counts or loss within this comparison.

Use a deliberately simple frozen policy: for each route, if the independently sampled training-negative outranking rate exceeds 0.15, prioritize the sampling action; otherwise prioritize the residual. These cutoffs are operational hypotheses, not calibrated thresholds. Order remaining actions deterministically and abstain to the common baseline if required diagnostics fail. Avoid using the twenty-user panel to tune this mapping. A future learned mapping requires separate tasks or complete trajectories for fitting and evaluation; four routes do not support credible cross-fitted policy-learning claims.

All arms start from the same prespecified strong SASRec incumbent and share the identical configuration set. Its training/evaluation cost must be charged equally as a common initialization charge and counted once in the global physical-cost ledger. Diagnostic guidance changes order only. Random search draws configurations uniformly without replacement from the same manifest. Match worker count, initialization, evaluation opportunities and stopping rules. A placebo arm computes the same diagnostics and prospectively permutes complete route-level guidance bundles, preserving repeated actions and temporal blocks. There are at most 24 route permutations, potentially fewer distinct assignments. Record the randomization mechanism, action frequencies and realized action changes. Identical guidance makes the placebo uninformative. Without route exchangeability, interpret this as a randomized policy perturbation or sensitivity analysis, not an exact permutation significance test.

Partition the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget before execution. Equal arm budgets include initialization charges, diagnostics, training, validation, debugging, failures and consumed resources of unfinished trials. Sum consumption across concurrent single-GPU trials; report elapsed wall time and CPU/LLM overhead separately. Use synchronized elapsed allocation time for each active GPU worker, rather than kernel-active time. Do not launch a trial unless its declared allocation fits the remaining allowance; stop at the deadline regardless of estimated completion. Only eligible host evaluations completed before cutoff update the incumbent; carry the previous incumbent forward and never backfill late results. Unfinished final HR@10 is missing, not a censored score bound. Record complete optimization traces and endpoint scores; if reporting area under the incumbent curve, use a fixed common budget horizon and a step-function incumbent beginning at the common baseline.

Repeat whole adaptive searches with paired search seeds only if the shared budget permits complete matched allocations; do not manufacture replication by treating categories or repeated actions as independent searches. Keep preprocessing/training/evaluation seeds at 0/42/42. Search-seed repetitions estimate search randomness, not training-seed robustness, and do not remove adaptive validation bias. Freeze methods and final selection before the host's held-out evaluation. Host macro validation HR@10 alone selects models; report per-category outcomes, coverage, completed trials, all costs and exploratory paired differences. Do not create an additional validation evaluator or modify pinned candidate sets.

Preserve original splits, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution per trial and the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Update the predictor writer and compatibility adapter for every architecture or scoring change so working/predict.py reconstructs exactly the trained model. No training, testing, filesystem inspection or benchmark improvement is claimed in this report.
idea.pseudocode:
freeze configuration_manifest, diagnostic_thresholds, priority_mapping
freeze search_seeds, worker_count, stopping_rules, budget_accounting
freeze common strong SASRec initialization and its equal arm charges
partition remaining global budget into complete matched arm allocations
for paired_search_seed in affordable_predeclared_search_seeds:
    for arm in [diagnostic_guidance, random_search, blocked_placebo]:
        initialize ledger and incumbent from common baseline
        if arm uses diagnostics:
            for dataset in four fixed routes:
                resolve and record five real training panel users
                report = DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)
                verify twenty-user full-catalog coverage across routes
                record instrumentation failures and charge all diagnostic cost
            priorities = frozen_mapping(report)
            # Example: training outranking rate > 0.15 => sampling first;
            # otherwise residual first; missing evidence => baseline deferral.
            if arm == blocked_placebo:
                priorities = prospectively_randomized_route_bundle_assignment(priorities)
                record permutation, preserved frequencies and realized action changes
        else:
            priorities = uniform_configuration_order_without_replacement(search_seed)
        while next complete trial allocation fits remaining arm allowance:
            train next manifest configuration using original splits and fixed seeds
            write architecture-consistent predictor and checkpoint
            obtain unchanged host validation evaluation
            charge training, validation, failures and debugging
            if eligible evaluation completes before arm deadline:
                update incumbent using host macro validation HR@10
            append incumbent and cumulative GPU cost to optimization trace
        stop active work at deadline; charge consumed resources
        retain previous incumbent for missing or late evaluations
report endpoint and anytime curves, category scores, coverage, costs and failures
report paired search differences only across completed matched repetitions
label search-seed uncertainty exploratory and separate from training robustness
freeze final selection before host-held-out evaluation

originality.positive: Combines coverage verification, predefined diagnostic-to-action mappings, blocked placebo guidance and full search-cost traces in a task-specific evaluation protocol.
originality.negative: Random-search benchmarking, placebo policies, anytime curves and gated interest mechanisms are established; the contribution is experimental integration rather than a new recommendation principle.

future_potential.positive: Can determine whether diagnostic guidance merits further investment and provide reusable action-outcome records for later policy research.
future_potential.negative: Four routes, a small fixed validation panel, uncalibrated mappings and limited affordable whole-search repetitions may leave effects inconclusive; validation gains do not establish immediate user utility.

code_difficulty.positive: The finite intervention menu reuses SASRec, existing scoring hooks and small localized architecture or sampling changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible manifests, panel repair, consistent predictor generation, deadline enforcement, shared initialization accounting, blocked randomization and repeated-search scheduling require substantial integration.

related_work.title: DeepMutation: Mutation Testing of Deep Learning Systems
contributions: Provides a precedent for checking diagnostics against deliberately altered models.
limitations: Does not establish SASRec-specific fault attribution or that mutation detection predicts beneficial training interventions.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not invalidate the task's pinned sampled-candidate objective, which remains the required selection metric.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces SASRec, the starting model family.
limitations: Does not establish benefits from an additional recent-history gate or diagnostic-guided search on these four datasets.

related_work.title: Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization
contributions: Establishes random search as a practical hyperparameter optimization comparator.
limitations: Fair application here requires matching configuration distributions, initialization, resources and stopping rules.

related_work.title: Hyperparameter Optimization: Foundations, Algorithms, Best Practices, and Open Challenges
contributions: Supports benchmarking complete optimization behavior and accounting for optimizer overhead.
limitations: Does not supply a validated diagnostic-to-intervention mapping for recommendation.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting performance-estimation bias.
limitations: Search-seed repetitions on the same validation split do not eliminate this bias.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses feature and instance gating to model sequential interests.
limitations: Its architecture is not the proposed gated SASRec residual and does not justify the proposed gate initialization.

related_work.title: Adaptive User Modeling with Long and Short-Term Preferences for Personalized Recommendation
contributions: Introduces SLi-Rec and adaptive fusion of long- and short-term interests.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed residual or diagnostic policy improves the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Reducing Overconfidence in Sequential Recommendation Trained with Negative Sampling
contributions: Combines more negatives with generalized binary cross-entropy to address overconfidence.
limitations: Changes loss and negative-count factors; comparisons must account for their additional computation.

related_work.title: Graph Neighborhood-based Negative Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides a graph-conditioned negative sampler using neighborhood overlap and a curriculum that limits likely false negatives.
limitations: Is not an explicit uniform/transition-successor mixture; it does not validate the proposed mixture or fallback.

related_work.title: Permutation Inference for the General Linear Model
contributions: Explains exchangeability restrictions and structured permutation schemes.
limitations: Four distinct dataset routes are not automatically exchangeable, and repeated actions do not create independent experimental units.
